answer_text:
Let \(a\) be the leading coefficient of \(P\), and define

\[
Q(x)=2P(x)-1.
\]

Then \(Q\) is also degree \(6\), and the condition \(0\le P(x)\le 1\) on \([-1,1]\) becomes

\[
-1\le Q(x)\le 1 \quad \text{for all } x\in[-1,1].
\]

If \(b\) is the leading coefficient of \(Q\), then \(b=2a\). So it suffices to find the maximum possible leading coefficient of a degree-\(6\) polynomial bounded in absolute value by \(1\) on \([-1,1]\).

Consider the Chebyshev polynomial

\[
T_6(x)=32x^6-48x^4+18x^2-1,
\]

which satisfies \(T_6(\cos\theta)=\cos 6\theta\). Hence \(|T_6(x)|\le 1\) on \([-1,1]\), and \(T_6/32\) is monic.

We prove the standard bound: if \(R\) has degree at most \(6\) and \(|R(x)|\le 1\) on \([-1,1]\), then the coefficient of \(x^6\) in \(R\) is at most \(32\) in absolute value.

Suppose \(R\) has leading coefficient \(c\) with \(|c|>32\). Set

\[
S(x)=\frac{R(x)}{c}.
\]

Then \(S\) is monic of degree \(6\), and

\[
|S(x)|\le \frac1{|c|}<\frac1{32}
\]

on \([-1,1]\). Now define

\[
F(x)=\frac{T_6(x)}{32}-S(x).
\]

Both terms are monic degree-\(6\) polynomials, so \(\deg F\le 5\).

Let

\[
x_k=\cos\left(\frac{k\pi}{6}\right),\qquad k=0,1,\dots,6.
\]

Then

\[
\frac{T_6(x_k)}{32}=\frac{\cos(k\pi)}{32}=\frac{(-1)^k}{32}.
\]

Since \(|S(x_k)|<1/32\), the value \(F(x_k)\) has sign \((-1)^k\). Thus \(F\) alternates in sign at the six ordered points

\[
x_0>x_1>\cdots>x_6.
\]

By the intermediate value theorem, \(F\) has at least one zero in each of the six intervals

\[
(x_1,x_0), (x_2,x_1),\dots,(x_6,x_5),
\]

so \(F\) has at least \(6\) distinct real zeros. This is impossible for a nonzero polynomial of degree at most \(5\). Hence \(|c|\le 32\).

Therefore for our \(Q\),

\[
b\le 32,
\]

so

\[
a=\frac b2\le 16.
\]

This bound is attainable: take

\[
P(x)=\frac{1+T_6(x)}{2}
=16x^6-24x^4+9x^2.
\]

Since \(|T_6(x)|\le 1\) on \([-1,1]\), we have \(0\le P(x)\le 1\) there, and its leading coefficient is \(16\).

Thus the maximum possible leading coefficient is

\[
\boxed{16}
\]
